transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-09
Time: 09:00 AM PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Laura (CTO - Pinegrove), Miguel (ML Eng), Nina (Product)

Summary:
Quick PLG/self-serve discovery focused on Redwood quickstart experience: time-to-first-token, free credits process, what customers can do with the hosted API versus when Dedicated/Private makes sense. Customer has a small ML infra team, wants to evaluate hosted first but has regulatory customers that may need private deployment later. Action items and next steps agreed at end.

Topics Covered:
- Quickstart and free credits flow
- Time-to-first-token metrics and typical onboarding steps
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs (latency, cost, data residency)
- Security: SOC 2, SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logs
- Pilot scope and success criteria (throughput, latency, hallucination tolerance)
- Next steps: trial account, benchmark, follow-up technical deep dive

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, do you all see my screen?
[00:03] Laura: Yep, looks good. Thanks Alex.
[00:05] Alex: Cool, I'm Alex, AE at Redwood, and Samir's our solutions engineer. Quick agenda — run through our quickstart flow, free credits and what you can get up and running with hosted, then dig into Dedicated/Private questions.
[00:16] Nina: Sounds great. We're mostly curious about how fast we can get a PoC running and what limitations we hit on the hosted side.
[00:20] Samir: Great, so Redwood PLG is designed around time-to-first-token — you can sign up, get free credits, and call the hosted API within minutes. Typical first call is a small prompt generation or embeddings job.
[00:31] Miguel: When you say minutes, is that literally from signup to our app calling the API? Or do we need to wait for approvals?
[00:37] Alex: For most teams, yes — signup, get API key, and start. Free credits are auto-applied for new accounts, for enterprise we sometimes need billing setup but that's later.
[00:45] Miguel: Nice. And how do you handle rate-limiting for the free tier? Like can we do a quick spike to test throughput?
[00:51] Samir: Free credits come with rate limits set to protect shared capacity — you can request higher limits for a short-term benchmark and we can temporarily lift them for a PoC. We'll help route that request.
[01:02] Laura: Our regulatory clients require data not to leave a region — does hosted support region pinning?
[01:08] Samir: Hosted API supports region routing; however, for strict data residency or air-gapped requirements, that's when Private comes in. Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and better isolation but still managed by Redwood.
[01:20] Nina: What's the typical latency difference between hosted and Dedicated? We're building a low-latency chat feature.
[01:25] Samir: It depends on model and size, but Dedicated reduces queuing variability because you have reserved GPU pools. For small-medium models 4k token context, median latency can drop 10-30% depending on batching. Hosted is optimized, though, and for many PLG use-cases it's sufficient.
[01:40] Miguel: Any ballpark on cost delta? If Dedicated gets us 20% lower latency, how much more expensive is it?
[01:46] Alex: Dedicated is priced as a reserved capacity contract — monthly commit. Unit cost per token can be lower if your volume justifies it, but there is the fixed commitment overhead. We'll sketch numbers after we see your expected qps and token mix.
[01:59] Laura: We're also concerned about security — SOC 2, SSO, KMS. Do you have SOC 2 docs and can we integrate with our SSO?
[02:06] Samir: Yes, Redwood has SOC 2 Type II. We support SAML/SSO for console access and RBAC. For encryption at rest, we integrate with customer KMS in Private deployments and have managed KMS in hosted. We'll share the compliance pack.
[02:20] Nina: Great. For the quickstart, what's a realistic end-to-end time to first token if we plug it into our app during the call?
[02:26] Alex: If you sign up now, I'd say you can get your first token in under 15 minutes — create account, get API key, follow the quickstart curl or SDK sample. We can share a dedicated quickstart doc link that has code snippets for your stack.
[02:39] Miguel: Any SDKs? We use Python and Node.
[02:42] Samir: Yep, official SDKs for Python/Node and community SDKs. The quickstart includes a minimal Python snippet: import client, client.generate(...).
[02:50] Laura: On data retention, hosted keeps logs for X days? Can we opt-out?
[02:54] Samir: By default we retain logs for operational troubleshooting — retention is configurable under enterprise plans and Private deployments can be customer-managed. We can share the exact retention windows in the security docs.
[03:06] Nina: If we wanted to run a benchmark, what would you need from us?
[03:10] Samir: A sample prompt set, expected qps, and target latency SLO. We can run tests on hosted first and then on Dedicated if you want reserved capacity comparisons. For reproducibility, share the sample dataset and we'll run against the same model variants.
[03:24] Miguel: We have about 50k unique prompts for retrieval-augmented generation; for the PoC we'd sample 5-10k. Is that workable on hosted?
[03:31] Samir: Totally workable; for heavy evals we might recommend lifting rate limits temporarily to avoid throttling. We'll coordinate.
[03:38] Laura: About private deployment — our legal team will ask about air-gapped installs. Do you offer on-prem packaging?
[03:44] Alex: Yes, Redwood Private offers VPC and an on-prem option. On-prem requires additional security review and a longer lead time — typically several weeks to months depending on complexity.
[03:56] Miguel: Could you give an example timeline?
[03:58] Samir: For a standard VPC/private control plane setup, customers onboard in 4-6 weeks. Full on-prem air-gapped can take 8-12 weeks with our operations team and your infra.
[04:09] Nina: Ok that helps. For the PLG flow, how do you prevent noisy neighbors on shared models? We've seen variability in other vendors.
[04:17] Samir: We use dynamic routing and autoscaling — and prefix cache techniques to improve cold-starts. For strict performance, Dedicated is best. Also we have per-customer soft and hard limits and can prioritize traffic by customer tier.
[04:30] Laura: Any mention of model variants — can we pin to quantized models to save cost?
[04:35] Samir: Yes, the catalog includes optimized quantized variants and we recommend them depending on latency/quality tradeoffs. Redwood Optimize provides recommended quantization profiles per workload.
[04:46] Miguel: For our team, the main success criteria for PoC are: 1) time to first token < 15 minutes; 2) baseline latency under 300ms P50 for small requests; 3) stable throughput at 20 qps with < 5% error rate.
[05:00] Alex: Perfect — we'll map those into a short pilot plan.
[05:03] (brief cross talk)
[05:06] Nina: One more question on billing — during free credits, do you get any invoice? We prefer to get usage visibility.
[05:12] Alex: You get a billing dashboard with token-level usage and cost breakdowns even during trial. We can also enable alerts.
[05:18] Laura: Can you demo the console quickly?
[05:20] Alex: Sure, Samir can share the console view.
[05:24] Samir: I'll just pull up the console — here is the per-route latency chart, token breakdown, and audit logs. (audio: Samir shares screen)
[05:38] Samir: You can see a route-level dashboard, and under settings we have API keys, SSO configuration, and a quickstart button to create a test API key and call the model from the browser.
[05:52] Miguel: That quickstart button — does it spin up any dedicated infra? Or is it purely hosted sandbox?
[05:58] Samir: Purely hosted sandbox backed by our shared capacity. It's safe for quick experiments. For realistic load testing we'd move to a controlled test account.
[06:08] Nina: For the free credits, is there an expiration window?
[06:11] Alex: Usually credits expire in 90 days but we can be flexible for enterprise pilots.
[06:16] Laura: Ok, I'm thinking about stakeholders — our security lead will want SOC 2 docs, our infra lead will want Dedicated pricing and capacity sizing, and product will want to run the quickstart for time-to-first-token.
[06:28] Alex: Great, we'll package that into a follow-up. Samir, can you own the sizing doc?
[06:33] Samir: Yep, I'll put together a Dedicated sizing estimate and a sample benchmark plan.
[06:38] Miguel: We'll provide sample prompts and expected qps. One ask — can you provision a trial account and give us an API key scoped for the benchmark?
[06:46] Alex: Yes, we'll provision a trial and add you as a project. You'll get the free credits and a test API key, plus instructions for the quickstart.
[06:53] (short pause)
[06:56] Nina: Any pitfalls you've seen with teams doing this quickstart?
[07:00] Samir: Biggest is mixing up keys and envs — use a dedicated test key and rotate it. Also selecting the right model variant up front avoids surprises on quality versus latency.
[07:10] Miguel: Sounds good. On model quality — do you offer eval tooling?
[07:14] Samir: Yes, Redwood Optimize includes evaluation suites and monitoring tied to prompt sets so you can detect regressions. We can enable that for your pilot.
[07:23] Laura: I think that's it for questions. Let's recap next steps.
[07:26] Alex: Recap — I'll send the quickstart guide, free credits instructions, and SOC 2/compliance pack by tomorrow. Samir will send Dedicated sizing and a benchmark plan. Pinegrove will send sample prompts and expected qps by 2026-07-12. We'll provision a trial account and invite your team.
[07:39] Nina: Works for us. Thanks everyone.
[07:41] Alex: Thanks — we'll follow up with meeting notes and the links.
[07:44] Miguel: Appreciate it.
[07:45] (call ends)
